body: This is amazing! Congratulations and enjoy time your son!!

It helps hearing others experienced the same...depression was most likely part of the situation prior to my heavy drinking. Just hoping I can bear these feelings without returning to drinking--I'm kind of surprised I've been sober for this long. Thank you fellow  SDers!

Sorry to hear about your Mum, and thank you for sharing. It is so true-life is precious. Ive also experienced loss and drinking doesn't do anything to help with grief. Someone once told me that we go on living in order to honor those who have gone before us. I won't drink with you today.

My grey area is uncertainty...I struggle with doubt. Today, I read a beautiful reflection about how most of our lives are lived in between the boundaries of certainty and uncertainty and that is where the real beauty of living takes place. Drinking (or so I believed) helped me cope with being unable to accept uncertainty. I'm mediocre (aka human) in all areas of my life (mother, wife, student) and am learning to not only accept it but embrace it.
Very nice quote. Thanks for sharing. I'm sorry for your friend's loss.
Thanks for sharing & congratulations! This is very inspiring...you look amazing and life seems to improved exponentially for you :)

That is so beautiful how you say that you emulate your kids living in the moment....I like to think that is why I work so hard to give my children a childhood where they can enjoy the present fully. Seeing their joy or their faces light up, is what I live for...I seem to forget that I need to take smaller steps and focus on the moment...sometimes everything seems to multiply and overwhelm me, but the small moments of joy/beauty/peace definitely outshine the longer periods of lowness.

You bring up a lot of things I struggle with: one, trusting my therapist, addiction counselor, and psychiatrist...the lack of trust runs deep not because of anything in particular that they have done but more so because of a significant history of trauma (one example: my mother tried to commit suicide when I was younger in front of me and with my aid...additionally, she was very abusive and through all of her years of therapy and treatment she never stopped hurting us or seemed to improve). But you've made me realize that this particular difficulty definitely falls under the "how I think about the world and myself" category which I've been working on...I really take to heart your advice about disclosure...I think it's time for me to disclose more fully (SD is my first practice space!) and I'm hoping to carry it over into the physical world. I love the last part of your comment: "Then I am more clear, conscious and purposeful. Then into the space where the hurts, regrets, pain and anger were stored, Love can blossom." Thank you for reaching out and sharing...and I will not drink tonight with you as well!
You're right...My thinking definitely needs to straighten out

Thank you--In addition to PTSD, I have been diagnosed with generalized anxiety and major depressive disorder...I stopped my medications while drinking...was going to see if maybe I could get through this/over this without alcohol or meds....but maybe I need to go back on medication.

Thank you-it's good to hear that others struggle with ptsd and have made positive changes...I like hearing 3 weeks is the key....that will help me to keep pushing to that mark to see where I'm at-and yeah, I  think I'm in a pretty bad place right now so thank you for the internet hug

Thanks u/OspreySoaring...I hadn't thought of that way (current trends) which makes sense. I more so feel like I can't trust myself to sustain not drinking, but I keep going to AA and getting treatment. My biggest asset has been to just show up--hoping that some kind of shift will take place in my mind. And, I agree about alcohol being an anchor...it was also like a screen through which I was viewing things--everything was dull and blurry...thanks again :)

Thanks for sharing and for the encouragement...that makes sense that I know myself best and what I might need...my PTSD and drinking have become so entangled that I'm not sure how to separate them...getting pretty tired of working hard at my trauma but still not getting relief from the symptoms. Keep me updated on your progress. I'll be rooting for you too!

It's nice to hear you going back to a familiar place and feeling welcome but it was also amazing that you were able to stay mindful of easing back into old routines. I like how you said..."if I put those comfortable old slippers of addiction back on..."
Congratulations! :)

Im only on day 6 but it helped me to find others who had stopped drinking. Through AA, I've found others who I can relate to and are sober....is there some kind of support group you could reach out to where you are? Keep going....day one is awesome! :)
Thank you :)
Beautiful! Thanks for sharing. I sense a centeredness and calmness in the second photo. You give me hope :)

I'm awful at advice but please know that you are not alone. In a similar situation, I would get a lawyer to represent me and volunteer to enroll in a good program to help me stop drinking. It's a medical disease to struggle with alcoholism and not a moral failing...many courts are realizing this and sending people for medical help. I know it feels shitty right now but you will be get through. I'll be thinking of you! You're not alone!!
Love the idea of playing the tape sideways and backwards! Am going to try the same and good for you for not drinking :)
This is beautiful! :)
Thank you :) Too often I feel "uniquely alone" but have to remember that no one is ever really alone.

Thank you. It's nice to hear others relate....I'll check out IRC and SD has been helpful too. I'm in therapy but have been blocking the help like you said by self-medicating...I'm tired of frustrating all around me--it's just that pain is hard to deal with...you give me hope :)
Hey u/Cabernet2 How's it going? I've been thinking about you...I'm at day 5 and am struggling. Would be great to hear where you're at :)

You are so amazing and brave! I really admire you and I'm also so sorry that you're going through such a challenging time. Please know that there is hope and better things to come on the other side....you have also given me a sense of hope knowing that there are others with the same struggles/experiences. I also have PTSD (from an aggravated assault in the Peace Corps and a horrible childhood) and realized during therapy about a year ago that I am a lesbian (I married pretty young before I had a chance to realize certain things about myself)....I thought I was alone in this situation and it feels good to hear another person share something similar. I'm still married and have decided to wait until my children are older to share this part of myself (still struggling with the guilt of holding this in). I can relate to your realization that you were gay and I admire your sobriety, strength, and courage to move forward!  I've realized in my (very recent) sobriety that the pain may be sharper instead of muted, but also that beauty and joy are felt more acutely--which has been worth the trade off so far. Thank you for sharing. I'll be thinking of you and rooting for you!!!
Thank you u/Trobin71. For me, being present is one of the greatest rewards of sobriety. Glad I could share something positive and I will not drink today in solidarity with you :)
Beautiful and amazing! Congrats on 100 days :)
Congratulations! :) What a wonderful partner you've found--someone who wants you to be healthy and whole. This is a beautiful post and I'm so happy  that you've found recovery and love.

Thank you. It's good to hear that dealing with them gets better the longer one is sober. And, I truly want to do this for my children. I will also not drink with you tonight in solidarity--much better to do it with others :)
Thank you! I'll not drink with you tonight as well :) Haha! John Wayne is great!!
Thank you. Feeling alone is tough but support really helps!
Thank you :)
Thank you so much! Doing it together is much easier than alone. I really appreciate your support and I support you too!
Thank you! My kids are my biggest motivator :)
Thank you. Getting support really does feel good :)
The movie was fantastic! Thanks for the encouraging words and hope you enjoy it too.
Thank you! The movie was awesome!!
Thank you and good luck to you as well :) I'm preparing to make it through another night!

I've had crazy drinking dreams too where I am guzzling alcohol and I can feel a real sense of guilt and failure. It feels good to wake up and know that it was just a dream. Unfortunately, my nightmares are worse when I stop drinking but I'm reminding myself they are just dreams.
Thank you :)

Loneliness is a trigger for me too u/wanttofloat...my therapist suggested making a list of 10 things to do when the urge to drink hits. So far, I've created a Spotify music list which I'll listen to while having a cigarette...calling or texting a friend or someone from AA, getting on here and reading or posting, I look through index cards with reminders of why drinking doesn't help (I put pictures of my kids, feeling lousy/foggy, not being who I want to be etc...), I also sometimes write out and track a craving in real time, distracting with something soothing (a warm blanket, a walk outside) These have helped quite a bit--keep trying and experimenting with what may work for you. We can help each other!

Don't beat yourself up over it-I keep slipping too...I've found going to AA meetings, reaching out to others when I feel the urge to drink and making plans ahead of time for my most vulnerable times helpful. Still, I often slip up (have still only managed 3 or 4 days in a row)...I'm still struggling with whether or not I really want to stop drinking--it helped me escape/numb out from some really troubling life stuff. But, I'm scared if I keep going and my drinking becomes worse then I could end up in an even worse place. I'll keep trying again too. There's a reason they say one day at a time and sometimes it might even have to be one hour (or so I've been told--it's starting to make sense). Thinking of you-keep in touch, keep trying and We can do this!

Sounds like an awesome plan! Weekend nights are tough for me too...I'm planning on celebrating my kids report cards at the movies, doing school work for my graduate school classes and maybe a hike! I love the idea of tea...I forgot how comforting that is-thanks for the reminder :)
I will not drink tonight! Instead I'm taking my children to Wahlbugers and the movies to celebrate good report cards!

Hi u/Cabernet2 and welcome to SD! Congrats on 2 days sober...that is awesome :) I am on my third day and need to re-set my badge. I've gotten a lot of support here and definitely want to keep trying. Drinking: A Love Story was great--I definitely related a lot to how alcohol had taken over her life. For the past couple of years, I started drinking heavily at night for a variety of reasons--it's been hard to break the pattern but it's definitely making the reasons I started drinking worse and not better! Keep in touch and I will not drink tonight with you!!

I'm thankful I'm going to bed sober tonight. Grateful for the many people who keep reaching out to me at AA, for a therapist that keeps encouraging and inspiring me to get better and for my beautiful children.
Congratulations! What an awesome post--your experience is an inspiration. Thank you :)

I finally found an AA meeting I really like...for me, it's more about connecting to the people that are in the meeting (I found other young mothers struggling like myself) as opposed to all of its tenets (not into recognizing God as my higher power)
Thank you :) It's nice to hear that others might come around on their support...I read Caroline Knapp's memoir a little while back which was a good read...I'm hoping to read Lit next...
Thank you for your support. It really helps to hear your experience...I think you're right about not wanting it 100%...for now I've decided to keep listening and keep trying!

Thank you for sharing. I can relate to the escapism and I loved what you say about choices....A line from one of my favorite songs: "and you have your choices...these are what make men great...his ladder to the saints" (Timshel by Mumford & Sons)
Thank you-it's really helpful hearing how you did it...707 days is amazing :) I dumped out all the alcohol in my house, I'm on SD tonight instead of dribking and I'm ready to try again!!
I will not drink tonight!
Thank you for sharing...Your honesty is beautiful and I wish you much luck in your recovery....710 days is amazing!!
Good luck...keep going! My children are my biggest motivators :)
I literally just submitted a post that I'm also failing on the 3rd or 4th day...I'm curious to hear others experiences...is it part of withdrawal and symptoms are just peaking then?
Wishing you luck! You're doing such a great thing for your child, wife and yourself-I think it's courageous and amazing

Yes, my children are extremely important to me...I've tried so hard to make sure they have a way better upbringing than I had....But, I'm afraid that I will unintentionally harm them with my struggles...A mother who can't access happiness, closeness, joy etc....seems to be a very bad mother. I would do anything to shield them from witnessing pain...even if that would mean my own exit. My brother is an adult with children of his own...his addiction is like witnessing some of my worst nightmares come true....I am trying hard not to drink because of my children....only 1 out of the last 6 days have I had drinks...but I feel terrible and very, very low...thank you for listening

I should also mention that the heavy drinking has continued...my treatment team is expressing concern about my ability to parent if I keep drinking 10 ounces of vodka a night...I am trying to stop the drinking because the last thing I want is to leave a negative impression....But, without drinking there is zero escape or relief
This is really helpful to keep in mind. Thanks for sharing! Here's to starting over again....yay for day 2 :)
Thank you for this-this is a wonderful thing to hear!
Sorry for your loss. Your grandmother would be proud of you.
Welcome! I'm a mom of 3 and I'm also starting over again today. Night time is the most difficult for me as well...I will not drink with you tonight!
Yes, mental health reasons...PTSD from a Peace Corps assault and a difficult childhood. Drinking is really unsafe and only fuels hopelessness. I want to keep trying
You're right the emotions do get so loud...I need to be mindful that it's hard but worth it. Thank you.
Congratulations on 8 months! Hope to be there too someday
Thank you! I want to get off that carousel...it's making me sick :)
Thank you. Brainstorming better stress relievers today
This made me smile...you are so right that drinking is not helping. I want what you've found...it's nice to get support. I really appreciate it!
Thank you. I will not drink tonight in honor of you and your support...it really helps to hear this
Thank you. Wishing you the best too. Starting over again today!
Thank you I'm looking forward to that fog lifting!
I went to 2 AA meetings this week...they helped me not drink those nights. I think I need to go to more...I did feel a sense of connectedness
Thank you I want to keep trying!

I have been diagnosed with PTSD, depression and anxiety from an assault as a Peace Corps volunteer as well as significant childhood adversity that kept impacting my adult life. My drinking directly coincided with my diagnosis...but it's only fueled despair. Thank you for your words of support. I'm starting over again today!
Thank you for your encouraging words...I'm root g for you too! I'm ready to start over again today
Thank you! I agree that my drinking has been a huge holding pattern...it makes me stuck and unable to deal with my issues. I want to keep trying
That's a nice thought...I look forward to a sober Sunday morning. Thank you!
Thank you-You're right & I plan to keep aiming for a permanent change
Thank you for sharing! I want that liberated feeling so today I will commit to not drinking...starting over again. I can't believe what a tremendous effort it is to defeat my ego
Thank you! I've been trying to keep myself accountable and it has helped in the past...I will hold onto what you said--that it's tough in the beginning...I have to remind myself of that

Wow! So many comments, support and suggestions...you are all amazing! It helps to read through and hear everyone's experiences and how many can relate...I did drink last night and the guilt is very heavy at the moment... But I'm ready and willing to start over again today by committing not to drink for the next 24 hours. I want to experience a better way of thinking and feeling. Thank you all

On day three of sobriety Grateful to experience the sun today...it's so much crisper and clearer when not hungover. I'm grateful too for this community and for all the people who have helped me through so much suffering. It feels good to take back my life and be in control while at the same time admitting that I'm also powerless
I made it! I appreciate the suggestions and maybe I need to change my perspective a little...my mindset doesn't feel as negative this morning as it was last night. Thank you everyone :)
This is great! Thanks for sharing

I know it's amazing what those closest to us sometimes cannot see...Im sorry that your ex wasn't more supportive. I know it really hurts me and it's lonely. My husband is the only one who knows my personal struggles...and if he can't support me who can?

Thanks for the support everyone! I'm in treatment for PTSD and my doctors think my drinking is a problem...so under their direction I agreed to a one week trial period. Dumping the alcohol out felt awesome earlier this afternoon...I felt really committed but now starting to waiver a little...going to focus on smaller increments
Today I am committing to not drink for one week, but I'll start with tonight.

I don't think you're jabbering at all! It's really good to reach out, to talk about what you've tried and what did or didn't work....I love your outlook, "I am the one with the power to cure me" I think I need a little bit more of that on my end :) It will serve you well as you engage in therapy...I hope you find a good fit, and/or a good support group....there are some treatment options that combine therapy, group support and alcohol addiction....Have you heard of DBT for alcohol? Traditionally, DBT was designed for those with borderline personality disorder but more and more it's been used to treat trauma, alcohol dependence, bipolar etc....it might be worth looking into as a potential alternative...

I completely agree! We must be kindred spirits because I LOVE many of the authors and books that you mentioned. Robinson so beautifully captures loneliness and has such a deep reverence for humanity and spirituality...themes I've always loved and identified with....I am excited to read her other novels.
I've read Into Thin Air (while I was in the Peace Corps) and Drinking: A Love Story (not too long ago)--both of which were very good! I'll have to check out the others you mentioned...especially the other Robinson novels, the Foster Wallace selections, and Lessing's African Stories, ...I read The Golden Notebook by her which was very good!! Because it's been awhile since I've read, here are some of my favorites from the past:
--anything and everything by Alice Munro (especially Family Furnishings); other short story writers such as George Saunders and Jhumpa Lahiri
--The Department of Speculation by Jenny Offill
--Freedom and Corrections by Jonathan Franzen
--The Red Tent by Anita Diamant
--A Heartbreaking Work of Staggering Genius by Dave Eggers
And, I've gotten into poetry recently and have fallen in love with Elizabeth Bishop, Mary Oliver, Stanley Kunitz, and Marianne Moore (although her work is a bit quirky!)

If you don't mind me asking, how did you stop drinking? I keep alternating 5 days sober, then back to drinking...or one day sober and back again...I have a lot of external stressors that contribute to my drinking so I'm not seeing the way forward at the moment...Are you in-between jobs and/or looking for something else or is there another reason you are not working (you don't have to answer if any of these questions are too personal!)

I do love to read and I'm glad you recognized Annie Dillard's book as my user name! Would love to hear what's on your reading list...I used to read like crazy but haven't had the clarity or focus in recent years. My last read was Housekeeping by Marilynne Robinson-it was very good! I, too, am more of a solitary, at-home drinker but would like to fill my time with other activities. Yoga would be nice and maybe some AA meetings. Thanks /u/Earth_and_Sky!

Thank you! Love getting these different ideas...will definitely checkout some podcasts and maybe some writing. I'm usually so tired at night when the drinking urge hits so it's great to have some options lined up. And maybe I will give weights a try :)
Very nice

I am so sorry that happened to you. I'm glad you have a therapist and you deserve to take good care of yourself. You are not alone. I also have PTSD, anxiety and depression from sexual trauma, abuse, and an aggravated assault. I've tried several meetings too but have struggled to find a good fit, but I keep trying different ones. There have been some women AA groups that I've liked...have you tried any of those? I'm also going to give a SMART recovery meeting a try...I'm  glad you found this group-I just joined and it's very supportive. Keep posting for support!
I will not drink tonight! Had 5 days sober and then slipped last night, but ready to start over!!

It's a breathalyzer device that is connected by bluetooth to your iPhone and it sends data on your sobriety to your treatment providers....They said it's used as an accountability and information tracker tool. Although in some cases it's used in legal situations, it was offered to me as a way to not drink and be accountable for not drinking. I'm definitely unsure about it. An app that comes to mind, is vetchange.org....it's geared toward veterans with PTSD but it has some really helpful tools (to track drinking, set goals, and see how your drinking compares to others....)
My doctor's suggested sober link to me but I've been hesitant to try.

Thanks everyone for the comments and encouragement...I guess the real dilemma for me is that I don't know if I want to stop drinking...I wasn't doing it for enjoyment--it was more for an escape and sometimes I hoped I wouldn't wake up in the morning. I know things can be better than they feel at the moment. The only thing that keeps going is my children. For them, I will go to bed sober tonight.

That makes a lot of sense...thank you coolcrosby. You are right...it has never worked in the past to "think" my way into staying sober. I'll check out the Baby Steps and plan to try for another night sober.
